ui.etsCardNote: One CBAM certificate covers 1 tonne of embedded CO₂e, priced at this rate. Only the EU importer buys them — mills and traders never do.
ui.etsPlainP1: This is the EU's carbon price. Emitting one tonne of CO₂ in the EU costs money: power plants and factories must hold a permit for every tonne they emit, and permits trade on the EU's carbon market — the Emissions Trading System (ETS). The market price of a permit is the number on this card.
ui.etsPlainP2: A CBAM certificate is the import version of an ETS permit. CBAM — the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism — is the rule that extends the same carbon cost to imported goods: the importer surrenders one CBAM certificate per tonne of embedded CO₂e, at the ETS price, so imported carbon costs the same as EU-made carbon.
ui.etsPlainP3: Who buys, where, when: only the authorised EU importer — the company responsible for the declaration — through the EU CBAM Registry, from February 1st, 2027. The price follows the ETS auction average — quarterly in 2026, weekly from 2027. Mills, producers, and trading houses never buy: they supply the data the declaration is built on.
ui.etsPlainP4: Why "cached": Kaimeter runs offline and never fetches prices on its own. This card shows the last price stored on this device (2026-04-07, the first published CBAM certificate price); correct it by hand at any time.
ui.etsPlainSummary: Plain words: what is this price? What is a CBAM certificate?

ui.packPreview: Pack preview — fields that will leave this device
ui.packRoleNoteExporter: Attach the mill records, verify the fields, and hand your buyer a clean data pack: emissions per CN code — no pricing, no internal data. You approve every export.
ui.packRoleNoteTrader: Packs pass through you: aggregate suppliers, check each order, and give every buyer its own pack. Supplier identity and pricing stay masked.
ui.packSealedNote: Exported from the served app, the pack is sealed: a W3C Verifiable Presentation signed with the mill's device key (Ed25519). The signature covers a fingerprint of the production evidence — a Merkle commitment, one hash that certifies every attached record. Change one number anywhere and the signature breaks; the buyer's machine proves it offline, contacting no one. From file:// it downloads as a plain demonstration JSON.
ui.packWorthDefault: Without verified data your buyer pays the +{m}% ({y}) mark-up — est. +€{x} on the same tonnage.
ui.packWorthNote: Estimate only — the buyer's bill also depends on the carbon price when they file and their Article 9 position. Commission defaults are conservative, so verified actuals usually save more than the mark-up alone.
ui.packWorthTitle: What your data is worth to your buyer
ui.packWorthVerified: Verified actuals avoid the +{m}% ({y}) penalty mark-up on {n} t — est. €{x} at the cached EU carbon price.
ui.packsSub: Emissions data per CN code, packed for your buyers. You approve every field that leaves.
ui.prefillNote: Prefilled from {f} — check against the source before saving.
ui.primerP1: CBAM — the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism — is the EU's charge on carbon in imports. From January 1st, 2026, iron & steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, and electricity imported into the EU carry a charge on the carbon emitted to produce them.
ui.primerP2: The EU importer pays — nobody outside the EU pays the EU directly. The importer buys CBAM certificates — one per tonne of embedded CO₂e, at the EU's carbon-market price — and files one annual declaration.
ui.primerP3: The bill is computed from the mill's data. Without verified data from the producer, the importer must use Brussels' conservative default values plus a penalty mark-up: +10% in 2026, +20% in 2027, +30% from 2028. Unverified data is the expensive option.
ui.primerP4: The charge is small now and grows every year. Who buys: only the authorised EU importer — the mill never buys. From whom: the European Commission, through the EU CBAM Registry. When: sales open February 1st, 2027; after that the importer buys whenever it suits during the year — there is no single purchase day. At what price: the EU ETS auction average, published per quarter in 2026 and per week from 2027 — it does not move in real time. The first surrender is due with the annual declaration on September 30th, 2027, and the payable share rises from 2.5% in 2026 to 100% by 2034.
ui.productionHint: Production log, outbound records, customs declarations — the net-tonne denominator and CN codes.
ui.reviewNote: The exporter submits the dossier; you review the evidence and mark the pack verified; the buyer's declaration then relies on it. Verification is one-way — nothing here is edited.
ui.reviewSub: The exporter submits the dossier; you review the evidence and mark the pack verified. Nothing is edited here.
ui.roleExporterDesc: Produce the data packs your buyers need — nothing leaves without your approval.
ui.roleImporterDesc: Track what you import, watch the 50-tonne line, project the certificate bill, prepare the filing.
ui.roleSub: Kaimeter renders the workflow for your role. You can change it anytime — the role button in the top bar.
ui.roleTraderDesc: Aggregate supplier packs, pass them through, keep per-buyer coverage.
ui.roleVerifierDesc: Open dossiers read-only; verify the evidence.
ui.sampleCodes: Sample CN codes for the demo — the full catalog seeds from the Commission workbook in the core.
ui.staled: Cached since 2026-04-07 (first published CBAM certificate price). Network sync when you connect.
ui.step1Hint: Three document classes make a complete CBAM dossier. Attach what is on the desk; nothing is uploaded anywhere — file names stay on this device.
ui.step2Hint: Every field below appears in the final record. Nothing is saved until you verify them in step 3.
ui.step3Hint: The same formulas as the declaration: mark-ups per year, the CBAM factor, exposure against the EU carbon price.
ui.step4Hint: Check each field against its source. The saved record exists only after you verify them all.
ui.tipCn: CN here means Combined Nomenclature — the EU's 8-digit customs commodity code that classifies the goods for the declaration. It is not the country code CN (China).
ui.tipDeadlines: Certificate sales open February 1st, 2027; the first annual declaration is due September 30th, 2027. All deadlines are Brussels time (CET/CEST).
ui.tipDossier: A complete CBAM dossier needs three document classes: energy & fuel bills, raw-material invoices with mill test certificates, and production output & customs records. The tags below show which classes you have attached.
ui.tipEmissions: Embedded emissions are the greenhouse gases released to produce one tonne of this product, in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent — the number the whole bill multiplies. Actual: from the mill's measured data, verified by an EU-accredited verifier. Default: Brussels' conservative published value for this CN code, carrying the penalty mark-up until verified.
ui.tipEts: This is the EU's carbon price — the market price of emitting one tonne of CO₂ in the EU, set by the EU's carbon market, the Emissions Trading System (ETS). CBAM certificates — one per tonne of embedded CO₂e in imported goods — are priced off that market and bought only by the authorised EU importer. Cached means the last price stored on this device: Kaimeter runs offline and never fetches anything — enter it by hand, or update it when you choose to connect.
ui.tipExposure: Estimated CBAM certificate cost for the selected year, and the two savings levers: verified mill data eliminates the penalty mark-up, and carbon price already paid abroad is deductible under Article 9. An estimate at the cached price — never a filing.
ui.tipLeaves: The exact fields written into the exported file — nothing else. The small grey key next to each label is the field name the buyer's system will read.
ui.tipMass: Your calendar-year total across all CBAM goods combined. Under 50 tonnes: no declaration — keep records only. Over the line: every tonne of the year becomes reportable. Electricity and hydrogen get no exemption and never count toward the line.
ui.verifyBad: Signature invalid — the file was altered, or is not a Kaimeter pack
ui.verifyHow: How this maps to the real world: verification is a regulated act, not a button. An EU-accredited verification body (accredited by a National Accreditation Body and listed in the EU CBAM Registry, per Delegated Reg (EU) 2025/2551) audits the dossier and issues a signed attestation — that attestation is what the importer's declaration relies on. Mark verified records exactly that act on the pack, and anyone can re-prove the seal offline with Verify a pack file.
ui.verifyLaterHint: Verification is not self-declared: after this dossier is reviewed, an EU-accredited verifier marks the pack verified (Verifier role → Review).
ui.verifyNeedsCore: Offline verification needs the Kaimeter core — open the served app (not file://).
ui.whatsNext: What happens next — no bill arrives. You buy CBAM certificates yourself, through the EU CBAM Registry (sales open 2027-02-01), and surrender them with one annual declaration — the first covers 2026 imports and is due 2027-09-30. Mills and traders never pay; they supply the data. The number above is an estimate — it moves with the carbon price when you buy and with your suppliers' verified data.
